findings.text: Display timing sync and scan behaviour is encoded as single-bit mode flags in low bits: positive and negative horizontal sync occupy bits 0 and 1, positive and negative vertical sync bits 2 and 3, interlace bit 4, double scan bit 5, composite sync variants bits 6 through 8, horizontal skew presence bit 9, double clock bit 12 and half clock bit 13. Two further bits are retained but marked obsolete for broadcast and pixel multiplexing.

Stereoscopic layout occupies a five-bit field starting at bit 14. Defined selectors run from none through frame packing, field alternative, line alternative, full side-by-side, depth based forms, top-and-bottom, and half side-by-side, with numeric selectors zero through eight. A mask covering that field allows extracting the layout independently of sync flags.

Picture aspect ratio and content type are small integer enumerations. Aspect uses none then 4:3, 16:9, 64:27 and 256:135 as values zero through four. Content uses no data, graphics, photo, cinema and game as values zero through four. Aspect values are also shifted to bits 19-22 to form mode flag selectors, with a four-bit mask covering that subfield.

A combined validity mask aggregates the supported sync, interlace, scan, clock, skew and stereoscopic bits while excluding aspect, obsolete and unrelated bits. Consumers can test mode flag validity by masking against this aggregate rather than enumerating individual bits.

Display power, scaling, dithering, dirty tracking, link health and panel kind use small integer codes. Power runs on, standby, suspend, off as zero to three. Scaling runs none, fullscreen, centered, aspect-preserving as zero to three. Dithering and dirty each use off, on, automatic or annotate variants as zero to two. Link status is good zero versus bad one. Panel kind is unknown, OLED and LCD as zero to two.

Plane orientation uses distinct bit groups: rotation selectors occupy bits zero through three for 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, and reflection selectors occupy bits four and five for horizontal and vertical mirroring. Separate aggregate masks cover rotation alone and reflection alone so callers can isolate each group.

Content protection state is undesired zero, desired one and enabled two. Field presentation uses bit zero for top field and bit one for bottom field. Cursor control uses one for buffer management, two for movement and three as the combined flag mask. Framebuffer dirty annotation uses one for copy, two for fill, three as flag mask, with at most 256 clips per request.

Encoder kinds run none through DPI as zero to eight. Connector kinds run unknown through USB as zero to twenty, covering VGA, DVI variants, composite, S-video, LVDS, component, DIN, DisplayPort, HDMI variants, TV, embedded DisplayPort, virtual, DSI, DPI, writeback, SPI and USB. Subconnectors use sparse values including automatic or unknown zero, VGA one, DVI-D three, DVI-A four, composite five, S-video six, component eight, SCART nine, DisplayPort ten, HDMI-A eleven, native fifteen and wireless eighteen.

Property typing combines legacy low bits with extended and atomic bits. Legacy bits mark range, immutable, enumerated, blob and bitmask kinds. Extended type occupies a higher bit range with object and signed-range selectors formed by shifting small type numbers. A high bit marks atomic-only properties. Object type tags use repeated-byte sentinels for CRTC, connector, encoder, mode, property, framebuffer, blob, plane, color operation, plus zero for any object.

Mode timing is a fixed record with pixel clock, horizontal display, sync start, sync end, total and skew, vertical display, sync start, sync end, total and scan count, refresh rate, flag and type words, and a fixed-length name. Resource enumeration returns pointer-sized addresses for framebuffer, CRTC, connector and encoder identifier arrays plus counts for each and minimum and maximum surface extents. CRTC setup carries connector list address and count, identifiers, framebuffer position, gamma size, validity flag and embedded timing record.

Plane placement separates destination and source geometry. The request carries plane, CRTC and framebuffer identifiers plus flags, signed destination origin with unsigned destination size to allow partial off-screen placement, and unsigned source origin and size expressed in sixteen-sixteen fixed point. Plane query returns current CRTC and framebuffer identifiers, a bitmask of compatible CRTC indices, an unused gamma field, a format count and address of a format array that excludes modifier-dependent formats, with a separate resource record listing plane identifiers and count.

Encoder query reports encoder and CRTC identifiers, encoder kind, and bitmasks of compatible CRTCs and cloneable encoders. Connector query carries addresses for encoder identifiers, mode records, property identifiers and property values, counts for modes, properties and encoders, current encoder and connector identifiers, connector kind and per-kind instance number, connection state, physical size in millimetres, subpixel order, and a zero pad word. Instance numbers are unique per kind but not stable across probe order.

Property description uses an enumeration entry of numeric value plus fixed-length name, and a property query with addresses for value and enumeration arrays, target property identifier, flag word, symbolic name, and counts for each array. Generic object property access uses addresses for identifier and value arrays with count, target identifier and type tag for reads, and value plus property, object and type for writes. Connector-specific property write carries value, property and connector identifiers. Blob access carries identifier, length and data address.

Legacy framebuffer creation carries identifier, dimensions, pitch, bits per pixel, depth and driver handle. Extended creation carries identifier, dimensions, four-character pixel format, flag word, and four entries each of buffer handle, pitch, offset and format modifier. Interlaced and modifier-present are single-bit flags; modifiers are ignored unless the modifier flag is set and all planes share one modifier. Dirty tracking carries framebuffer identifier, flags, fill color, clip count and clip address. Mode attachment pairs a connector identifier with a timing record.

Cursor control carries flags, target CRTC, signed position, size and driver handle; the extended form adds signed hotspot coordinates. Gamma lookup carries CRTC identifier, table size and three addresses for red, green and blue channels. Color transforms use nine-element and twelve-element arrays of sign-magnitude fixed-point coefficients for three-by-three and three-by-four mappings. Lookup entries pack red, green, blue and reserved fields in sixteen-bit or thirty-two-bit forms, with sixteen-bit values linearly spanning zero to full intensity. A size hint holds sixteen-bit width and height.

Color operation kinds form an ordered enumeration: single curve applied to all channels, uniform one-dimensional table of thirty-two-bit entries, three-by-four matrix, scalar multiplier in fixed point, and three-dimensional table of thirty-two-bit entries. Table payloads travel as blobs with driver-advertised size; cubic tables use row-major traversal with red fastest then green then blue. Interpolation selectors currently define tetrahedral handling for three-dimensional tables and linear handling for one-dimensional tables.

Enumeration follows a count-plus-address pattern where the caller supplies storage addresses and receives counts, with property names as the stable recognition key. Connector instance identity is the pair of kind and per-kind number, not the object identifier. CRTC compatibility is an index-based bitmask. Source cropping uses fixed-point units while destination placement permits negative origins. Reserved and pad words must be zero and several gamma and format fields are defined as unused or restricted.

Several values are obsolete or restricted and must not be used for new behaviour: broadcast and pixel-multiplex timing bits, the pending property bit, and gamma or format paths marked never used or modifier-free. Extended and atomic property bits change interpretation of legacy type bits, and color matrices use sign-magnitude rather than two complement representation, so naive signed arithmetic would misinterpret coefficients.
